```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
stopifnot(requireNamespace("nlme", quietly = TRUE))
```

## Fit an nlme measurement model

The paper uses `nlme` for its primary measurement models. The public REPAIR
workflow now accepts a fitted, single-group linear `nlme::lme()` model:

```{r quick-start}
growth <- nlme::lme(
  Reaction ~ Days, random = ~ Days | Subject,
  data = lme4::sleepstudy, keep.data = TRUE
)
people <- data.frame(Subject = levels(lme4::sleepstudy$Subject),
                     observed = seq_len(18))  # illustrative predictor
repair_effects(list(growth = growth))
fit <- repair(re("Days", "growth") ~ observed,
              list(growth = growth), people, id = "Subject")
summary(fit)
```

`repair_effects()` lists scalar random coefficients; `repair_data()` computes
and aligns their likelihood-only scores and error covariance by person ID;
`repair()` performs that assembly and fits M-MOM. These functions have the same
interface for lmer and lme inputs. Scores remain deviations from fixed effects,
and observed structural variables are treated as error-free.

The summary identifies the measurement backend. For nlme, singularity is not
assessed using lme4's criterion. Inspect the measurement fit and warnings issued
when fitting it. An available nlme `apVar` failure message is retained as a
variance-parameter uncertainty diagnostic; its absence is not a convergence test.

## Supported covariance structures

| Component | Supported |
|---|---|
| Measurement model | Linear Gaussian lme, one grouping factor |
| Residual correlation | Independent, `corAR1`, `corCAR1` |
| Residual variance | Constant, `varIdent`, `varPower` |
| Combined structures | Supported correlation plus supported variance function |
| Retained data | Explicit data frame, `keep.data = TRUE` (the lme default) |

AR(1) objects that nlme converts to `corARMA(p = 1, q = 0)` for irregular integer
times are supported. This does not admit arbitrary ARMA orders. Correlation
groups must match the random-effect group; finer subgroup correlations,
multilevel lme fits, nonlinear nlme fits, and other variance/correlation classes
fail explicitly. `varComb` and other combinations of variance functions have
not yet been admitted. Contained lmer nuisance groups are supported separately;
see `vignette("nested-nuisance")`. Shared nuisance levels remain rejected.

The fitted covariance includes the residual scale and variance-function weights.
In particular, `varPower(~ fitted(.))` uses the weights retained by the fitted
model; recomputing them from final fitted values can differ at convergence.
The covariance is residual covariance, not posterior BLUP covariance and not the
full marginal covariance including the target random effects.

## Why observation alignment matters

An lme object's source data, effective fitting rows, and public response extractor
need not have the same length when `subset` or `na.exclude` is used. REPAIR uses
the effective observation IDs saved in the fitted object's grouping information,
then aligns its retained data, fixed/random designs, response, and covariance.
It preserves fitted contrasts even if session contrast options change. It also
checks that the reconstructed designs reproduce the saved fitted values.

Do not remove or edit the model's retained data. If it was fitted with
`keep.data = FALSE`, refit with retained data. The extractor does not re-evaluate
the original data expression or subset in the current workspace. Structural
omission is still a separate decision: `na_action = "omit"` refers to people in
the structural cohort and retains their exclusion reasons.

## Reproduce reference results from repeated observations

The package bundles three deterministic synthetic datasets. Expected results
come from the paper's production scoring and M-MOM functions, cross-checked
against an independent algebra implementation. No repair functions were used to
generate these expectations. These are per-dataset agreement checks, not the
paper's published simulation tables or evidence of Monte Carlo coverage.

```{r references}
reference <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "nlme-workflow-reference.rds", package = "repair"
))
reference$provenance[c("source_commit", "nlme_version",
                     "preliminary_moment", "variance_bread")]
names(reference$cases)
```

The balanced predictor case starts with raw repeated observations, fits the
measurement model, and predicts an observed distal outcome from its intercept
and slope scores:

```{r reproduce}
case <- reference$cases$predictor_balanced
growth <- nlme::lme(y ~ z, random = ~ z | id, data = case$data,
                    control = nlme::lmeControl(msMaxIter = 300))
fit <- repair(
  distal ~ re("(Intercept)", "growth") + re("z", "growth"),
  models = list(growth = growth), data = case$people, id = "id"
)
actual <- tail(fit@struc_fit@coefficients, 1)[,
  c("estimate", "se", "ci_low", "ci_high")]
rownames(actual) <- NULL
rbind(package = actual, production_reference = case$focal)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(actual, case$focal, tolerance = 1e-5)))
```

For a same-model outcome/predictor-error example with heterogeneous AR(1)
residuals:

```{r correlated}
case_cor <- reference$cases$both_ar1_ident
growth_cor <- nlme::lme(
  y ~ z, random = ~ z | id, data = case_cor$data,
  correlation = nlme::corAR1(form = ~ time | id),
  weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | phase),
  control = nlme::lmeControl(msMaxIter = 300)
)
fit_cor <- repair(re("z", "growth") ~ re("(Intercept)", "growth"),
                  list(growth = growth_cor), case_cor$people, id = "id")
head(fit_cor@analysis_data@err_xy)  # retained cross-error covariance
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(coef(fit_cor)),
  case_cor$coefficients$estimate, tolerance = 1e-5)))
```

The test suite also refits the unbalanced outcome-error case and compares
coefficients, covariance, SEs, and confidence intervals on both R and C++
backends. Separate tests construct GLS and residual covariance analytically for
shuffled/missing/subset observations and the supported residual structures.

## Match the reporting scale

`repair()` returns estimates on the supplied input scale. The frozen production
comparisons use the primary modified-moment estimator with
`skip_internal_scaling = TRUE`. They do not invoke the simulation's alternative
internal latent-SD standardization or alpha-search variants.

The simulation's `vh_study2.R` applies the generating population slope SD after
estimation. For the bundled predictor case that known SD is 0.8:

```{r scale}
reported <- actual * case$reporting_scale
rbind(package = reported, population_SD_reference = case$reported_focal)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(reported, case$reported_focal, tolerance = 1e-5)))
```

Estimates, SEs, and both CI endpoints must be scaled together. An empirical
application does not have a known generating population SD; do not substitute
the SD of noisy scores without defining the intended estimand. The package
performs no automatic standardization.

All inference here remains conditional on fitted measurement-model parameters,
uses the model-based normal-error covariance, and assumes independent analysis
people. Adding nlme support does not change those assumptions or propagate
first-stage parameter uncertainty. Provenance and regeneration instructions are
in the bundled `extdata/README.md` and the repository's `dev/nlme-validation.md`.
